title: Reverb on a send
learned: A send effect is shared: each channel's SEND decides how much of it goes in
SEND A out of the console → effect → RET A back into the console
On a send the effect plays only wet (MIX fully up): the dry sound is already in the mix
Reverb is the room around the sound: more send = further away

steps.why: Reverb puts sounds in a room. In a real room everything shares the same space, so instead of one reverb per sound, the console sends a bit of each channel to one shared reverb and mixes its output back in. That is a send effect, and each channel decides how much it sends.
steps.do: The melody (channel 1) and the drums (channel 2) play. A reverb (JX-REV) is in the rack. Press Next.

steps.why: SEND A of the console carries the sum of every channel times its SEND A knob.
steps.do: Drag a cable from SEND A of the console to IN L of the reverb.
steps.after: Nothing yet: all SEND A knobs start at zero, and the reverb's output goes nowhere.

steps.why: The reverb's stereo output comes back into the console's RETURN A, which goes into the master.
steps.do: Drag OUT L of the reverb to RET A L of the console, and OUT R to RET A R.
steps.after: The loop is closed: console → SEND A → reverb → RET A → console.

steps.why: The dry sound already reaches the master through the channels. On a send, the reverb should give only its tail.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn MIX of the reverb fully up.
steps.after: MIX at 100 % means only wet. If you left it lower, the reverb would add the dry sound a second time.

steps.why: Now each channel chooses how much room it gets.
steps.do: Press F3 and turn SEND A of channel 1 (the melody) up.
steps.after: The melody now sits in a hall, the drums stay dry and close. More send sounds further away.

steps.why: Different amounts of the same room give a mix depth.
steps.do: Turn SEND A of channel 2 (the drums) up just a little, then press Tab.
steps.after: Both sounds share one room now, the melody further back than the drums: front to back, like on a stage. One reverb serves every channel; adding a channel costs only a knob.
steps.try: In the rack, turn DECAY of the reverb for a longer tail, and flip ROOM / HALL / PLATE for other spaces.

steps.do: Insert for one sound, send for a shared space: that is how effects meet in a mix. Press Next to finish.
